In M ἀτίται [without honor] with a small line above the a, by which the dative is indicated ἀτίτᾳ [to the one without honor], which would be said for ἀτίτῳ [to the one without honor], not for ἀτίτῃ [to the one without honor], since the Doric form has no place in these anapaests. But Aeschylus undoubtedly intended the nominative to be ἀτίται [without honor], although nouns of this kind in -ης are rarely used in a passive sense, on which see Lobeck on Sophocles Ajax 241. To this is added that ατίτας [without honor] (Doric for ἀτίτης [without honor]) is used for one who has not paid the penalty or is unpunished, Eumenides 250 μὴ λάθῃ φύγδα βὰς ματροφόνος ἀτίτας [lest the matricide escape notice, going into exile, unpunished]. Hesychius interprets ἀτίτην [without honor] among other things as unavenged and dishonored.
But we, without honor, with old flesh, left behind from that help, remain.

Thus I corrected for Ἄτλανθ᾿ ὃς αἰὲν [Atlas who always], on which see the Oxford annotation. The scholiast is right, except that he did not notice that the letter e should be deleted, saying: the many, not knowing (the genitive form Ατλα [of Atlas]), here say 'Ατλαντα [Atlas], not knowing that the θ is there.
